answer: Operator Liability Cipher. Each identity registers with a hardware cipher that signs its actions under a rotating key tied to the operator's real hardware. If any node on the operator's device sends a malformed pulse—flagged by a lightweight sparrow check that samples neighbors—the operator's entire key set is revoked, not just the offending wallet. Rewiring costs a full hardware replacement plus reissuing every identity, so running N sybils means N device swaps and lost reputation, paid each time.
